rationale: C04 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both directives address the Chairman of the Civil Aeronautics Board, describe presidential review of a Board recommendation in an international aviation case through foreign-policy, defense, and broader national-interest considerations, decline approval because the supporting record does not adequately resolve economic or public-interest concerns, and explain the deficiencies before returning or withholding approval. This combination of shared language, audience, decisional posture, and administrative machinery is materially stronger than mere topical similarity. C16 and C19 share the CAB-review setting and some procedural structure, but their language and operative logic are less closely aligned.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I have reviewed the case on the basis of foreign policy and defense considerations together with other elements of the national interest that are within my particular responsibilities
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I have reviewed the Board's recommendations in the Service to Regina Case on the basis of the broad national welfare, foreign policy and defense considerations, and other matters within my special responsibilities.
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive near-parallel formulation of the President's special review criteria for an international CAB determination.

shared_material.child_excerpt: have decided (a) to approve the Board's denial of applications and ( b ) to withhold my approval in other respects
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am compelled to return the Board's proposed order without my approval.
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same presidential approval mechanism to reject all or part of a proposed CAB disposition.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the number and breadth of the proposed certificates imply a potentially serious economic impact upon the existing overseas and foreign route operations of United States carriers. This concern is not met by the record now before me.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: These questions are not intended to be exhaustive but only to suggest the difficulties of judging the public interest in this international case in the absence of policy and findings more closely defined than I find in the record before me.
shared_material.explanation: Both justify nonapproval by identifying unresolved economic concerns and finding the Board's record inadequate to support the proposed international certification.
